name: Shape Detection: BarcodeDetector
plain: Finds and reads barcodes and QR codes in an image or camera frame.
meaning: Turns pixels into decoded strings (product codes, URLs, tickets). Runs on-device with no prompt, once the page has the image.

access.prompt_ui: None for the API; camera needs getUserMedia prompt
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

edge.note: Supported on macOS only. Before Chrome 113, on macOS Ventura (13) and above, this interface silently failed. See <a href="https://crbug.com/40245611">bug 402456

data.metric: Finds and reads barcodes and QR codes in an image or camera frame.

fields.name: format
fields.range: qr_code, ean_13, code_128, aztec, pdf417, data_matrix and more (about 14)

limits.headline: Can find barcodes and QR codes in a picture or camera view
limits.user_action: You tap Scan QR code and allow your camera, or you pick a photo.
can: Find a barcode or QR code in a photo
Scan live from your camera, once you allow it
Tell the page what the code says
cannot: Use your camera without its own camera permission
Scan in Firefox or in Safari without a special setting
Always find codes in a blurry or tilted image
See the rest of your camera roll
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Android Chrome support it, though not on every device. Safari and Firefox lack full support.

story.what_it_is: A page can read barcodes and QR codes from a picture or the camera.

marketing.name: Shape Detection API
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs describe the API as a way to detect barcodes, faces and text in images.

story.for_you: You hold your camera to a QR code or barcode and the page reads it in a flash. The camera still asks permission first.
story.for_makers: Makers can scan tickets, products and payments without a native app, using the camera you already approved. The reading runs on your device so images do not need to leave it.

use_cases.example: A store site scans a barcode to look up a product in the aisle.
An event site scans tickets at the door with a phone.
A payments site scans a QR code to pay.
An airline site reads a boarding pass code.
A warehouse web tool scans shelf labels and counts stock.
A phisher puts a fake QR code on a flyer that leads to a bad site.

technical_bounds: Format list varies by OS (Android, ChromeOS, macOS; Windows partial)
FaceDetector and TextDetector exist only behind flags
